mode_evidence: Begins with physical gazing at the setting sun, then the image must 'remain clear and fixed, whether thine eyes be shut or open'; later steps (water, ice, lapis ground) are imagined ('thou shouldst imagine'), yet the text says the ground 'will be seen'. Later meditations are cued to 'the mind's eye', so the sutra spans afterimage-like retention and constructed imagery without marking a perceptual threshold.
onset_evidence: The first step is a method for someone who sees nothing: gaze at the sun about to set, fix the mind, keep the image after looking away. Stages then build step by step; the digest shows no time scale and no statement that light cannot be forced. Section 11 (dimly seen versus samadhi) was not in the digest.

conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Gaze at the sun when about to set and like a suspended drum.
conditions.prerequisites: Steady, unscattered thought; each stage completed before the next.

stages.label: First Meditation: sun
stages.description: Setting sun held until it stays clear whether eyes are shut or open.

stages.label: Second Meditation: water
stages.description: Clear water, then ice, then lapis lazuli ground, transparent within and without, jewels with rays of many colours.

stages.label: Ninth Meditation: Amitayus
stages.description: Begin with the white hair-twist between the brows; the signs and marks 'naturally appear before their eyes'.

what_to_do_with_light: Stabilise the image so it persists eyes shut or open, never allow thought to scatter, then build further scenes from it; clear and distinct, like seeing the palm of one's hand.
obstacles_and_fixes: Scattered thought: do not let it be lost; hold the image fixed.
cautions: Meditation of another kind than the prescribed is called heretical meditation.
interpretation: The visions are a rehearsal of the Pure Land and of Amitayus as a samadhi of remembering the Buddhas, leading to rebirth there.
practice_summary: Sit facing west and watch the sun as it is about to set, looking like a suspended drum, with the mind fixed and unwavering. Then make that image stay clear and fixed whether your eyes are shut or open. Next take clear water, then ice, then imagine its lapis lazuli ground, transparent and shining within and without, with jewels sending out rays of many colours; keep each image from scattering. Build outward from there in order, tree by tree and lake by lake, then to the Buddha, starting with a single mark, the white hair-twist between the eyebrows, held as clearly as possible, whereupon the remaining marks are said to appear of themselves.

key_passages.anchor: gaze upon it (more particularly) when it is about to set and looks like a suspended drum
key_passages.paraphrase: The practice starts from actual gazing at the low setting sun.
key_passages.quote: gaze upon it (more particularly) when it is about to set and looks like a suspended drum.

key_passages.anchor: let (that image) remain clear and fixed, whether thine eyes be shut or open
key_passages.paraphrase: The image must persist after the eyes leave the sun, with eyes closed or open.
key_passages.quote: After thou hast thus seen the sun, let (that image) remain clear and fixed, whether thine eyes be shut or open;

key_passages.anchor: gaze on the water clear and pure, and let (this image) also remain clear and fixed
key_passages.paraphrase: Water is perceived next, then ice, then lapis lazuli ground with jewels and rays of many colours.

key_passages.anchor: the eighty-four thousand signs and marks will naturally appear before their eyes
key_passages.paraphrase: Hold one sign, the white hair-twist, as clearly as possible; the rest then appear on their own.

confidence_note: Digest only; section 11 on 'dimly seen' versus samadhi vision was not in the digest and is taken from the search agent's hint, unconfirmed.
